title: How it works
description: A full walkthrough of the Mad Devs test assignment: every requirement, the recruiter’s clarifications and the author’s decisions — what is done, how it works and how to check it.

sections.title: In short
items: A booking interface for one meeting room during the working day 09:00–18:00 on weekdays: pick a date, see the day timeline, create, edit and delete bookings.
All 8 business rules of the assignment plus the recruiter’s clarifications are checked by one function — in the form (instantly) and on the mock server (final word).
Conflict 409 is handled as point 8 requires: a clear message, a refreshed list, no lost input.
Stack: Next.js 16, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, TanStack Query, axios, zod, react-hook-form, zustand, next-intl. Architecture — Feature-Sliced Design.
Quality: 22 unit tests, 19 e2e scenarios (Playwright, desktop and mobile), axe accessibility checks (WCAG 2 AA), FSD architecture linters.

sections.title: 1. Task (assignment)
items: Build a meeting room booking interface within a working day. Working hours are 09:00–18:00.
The user can: pick a date; see existing bookings for that date; choose start and end time; create a booking; edit a booking; delete a booking.
Display format is up to the developer: list, timeline, slot grid or day calendar. Chosen: a day timeline — booking blocks by time, a 30-minute grid, a red line for the current time.
Timebox 4–6 hours; deliver: repository, README (how to run, what is done and not, time spent), deployed demo, AI chat log.

sections.title: 2. What the app does
items: Date selection: ← → by day, a calendar (popover on phones, a month calendar on the left on wide screens), a “Today” button.
Bookings of the day on a 09:00–18:00 timeline; long titles wrap onto the next lines inside the block.
Create: the “New booking” button (first free time), a click on a free cell or a mouse-drag range.
Edit: click a booking — date, time and title can be changed; after saving the schedule switches to the booking date.
Delete: the “Delete” button in the form, then a confirmation with date, time and title.
Occupied time is disabled in the form: you cannot pick a start or end that overlaps another booking.
Day summary: number of bookings, how much time can actually be booked, the next free time (click opens the form).
The selected date lives in the URL (/?date=2026-10-23): survives a reload, can be shared.
Keyboard shortcuts: ← → previous/next day, T today, N new booking.
Language RU (main) and EN, theme — system, light or dark; switches in the header, the choice is remembered.
Neighbouring days are prefetched — arrows are instant; while a day loads, the previous schedule stays dimmed and inactive.
A custom 404 page in the interface language.

sections.title: 3. Business rules and their implementation
items: 1. Start and end within 09:00–18:00. Options outside the day are not offered; the server responds 422.
2. start < end. Ends before the start are disabled; the server responds 422.
3. Minimum duration 30 minutes. Shorter is unavailable in the form; the server responds 422.
4. Maximum duration 2 hours. Longer is unavailable in the form; a mouse drag does not stretch beyond 2 hours.
5. Bookings cannot overlap; touching borders is fine (10:00–11:00 and 11:00–12:00). Occupied time is disabled in the form; the server responds 409.

6. Past time cannot be booked. A past date is read-only (create disabled, banner). Today the start is no earlier than the next 15-minute step: at 14:20 the first start is 14:30. Seconds count: a 14:15 booking has started at 14:15:40.
7. When editing, a booking does not conflict with itself — it is excluded from the overlap check.

8. The server may return 409 even if the UI considered the slot free. The UI shows a clear message in the form, refetches the bookings (the other booking appears on the timeline) and keeps the form open — input is preserved. The form cannot be closed while saving, so the response is never lost.

Additionally (recruiter answers): weekdays only (Mon–Fri); 15-minute step (10:07 → 422); bookings that started or ended cannot be changed or deleted (lock on the block, server — 422). A non-existent date (Nov 31) → 400.
All rules are one function, findRuleViolation, shared by the form and the mock server. It returns a violation code; the text is added in the interface language. The rules are covered by unit tests.

sections.title: 4. “What matters” (assignment)
items: Business logic and validation: one rules function + zod schemas for the form and the API; the error is shown under the specific field and linked to it for screen readers.
UI states: loading — a skeleton of the same shape; empty — a hint; error — a message and “Retry”; submitting — a spinner and disabled buttons; a failed background refresh keeps the schedule.
Server errors: 400 (format), 404 (already deleted — toast and refresh), 409 (conflict), 422 (rule violated), offline — clear messages in the interface language, including zod texts.
API and UI are separated: component → hook → entities/booking/api → axios. Responses are validated with zod. Switching to a real API is the NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL variable.
Readable TypeScript and structure: strict, types inferred from zod, Feature-Sliced Design with automated checks (ESLint layer boundaries, steiger, fsd-check, Tailwind class check).

Responsive and accessible: layouts for phone, tablet, laptop and monitor (checked at 13 widths 320–2560); keyboard support, focus returns after dialogs close, screen reader labels, WCAG 2 AA contrast (axe in e2e).

sections.title: 5. Layout by screen width
items: Phone (below 640 px): one column — date, full-width “New booking”, banner, summary chips, timeline.
Tablet (640–1023 px): date navigation and “New booking” on one row.
Laptop and desktop (1024 px and up): two columns — month calendar, “New booking”, summary and shortcuts on the left; date heading with arrows and the timeline on the right.
Monitor (1440 px and up): the UI scales smoothly (≈17 px at 1920, ≈19 px at 2560), wider container.
One markup for all widths: block order changes with Tailwind classes, no duplication.

sections.title: 6. Stack and architecture
items: Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, strict TypeScript.
UI: Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui (Radix), lucide icons; theme — next-themes.
Data: TanStack Query 5 + axios; forms: react-hook-form + zod 4; screen state: zustand; dates: date-fns; translations: next-intl.

Feature-Sliced Design: app/ — re-exports only; src/_app (providers, header, mock API), src/_pages (booking, about, not-found), src/entities/booking (schemas, requests, rules), src/shared (http, errors, time, UI kit). Translations live in the owning slice.
Tests: vitest (rules, grid, drag range, summary) and Playwright (CRUD, 409, past date, weekend, load errors, language, 404, shortcuts, mouse drag, theme, accessibility).

sections.title: 7. Mock API (assignment contract)
items: GET /api/bookings?date=YYYY-MM-DD → 200 Booking[] | 400
POST /api/bookings → 201 Booking | 400 | 409 | 422
PATCH /api/bookings/:id → 200 Booking | 400 | 404 | 409 | 422
DELETE /api/bookings/:id → 204 | 404 | 422
Booking = { id, date: YYYY-MM-DD, start: HH:mm, end: HH:mm, title? }
Error: { code, message, field? } — 409 overlap, 422 rule violated, 404 deleted, 400 bad format. The text follows Accept-Language.
X-Time-Zone — the browser time zone: the server uses it to determine “now”.
Implemented with Next.js Route Handlers and in-memory storage. A real backend, auth and database are not required by the assignment.

sections.title: 8. Clarifications from the Mad Devs recruiter

qa.q: Which time zone defines working hours and past time?
Bookings Mon–Fri only or any day?
It is 14:20 — start at 14:20 or at the nearest future time?
Can a booking that has started or ended be edited or deleted?
Is a 15-minute step enough or is arbitrary time needed?
When editing, can the date be changed or only time and title?
Is a random 409 from the mock server fine to demonstrate the conflict?
Keep data in memory if it resets after a restart?
Should public holidays be taken into account?
In what format should the AI chat be submitted?
Documentation, auth, language, tests, booking horizon, extra features?

sections.title: 9. Author’s decisions
items: No authentication (assignment: “auth is not required”): any user can change or delete any booking.
Booking time is stored without a time zone (HH:mm) — everyone is in one office; the browser zone defines “now” and is sent to the server.
Holidays are ignored, no booking horizon limit, the title is optional (up to 80 characters).
Conflict 409 is reproducible: the mock returns 409 for about every fifth create (MOCK_CONFLICT_RATE=0.2) and puts a “Taken by a colleague” booking there. It is a simulation, not a bug.
Data lives in server memory. On Vercel the server runs as several instances with their own memory, so a booking may occasionally “disappear” after a refresh; a real backend does not have this.
Saving waits for the server (no optimistic display), deleting goes through a confirmation — point 8 is handled more reliably this way.
Beyond the assignment: RU/EN, dark theme, date in the URL, mouse-drag selection, day summary, keyboard shortcuts, day prefetching, responsive layout up to 2560 px, this documentation page.
Tests: unit — rules and calculations; e2e — all key scenarios and accessibility.

sections.title: 10. How to check manually
items: Create: click a free cell (or drag a range with the mouse) → the form with that time → “Book”.
Edit: click a booking → change date, time or title → “Save”.
Delete: click a booking → “Delete” → confirm.
Conflict 409: create bookings — about every fifth gets 409; the message appears in the form, “Taken by a colleague” appears on the timeline, your input stays. It is a simulation, not a bug.
Overlap: occupied time is disabled in the form; through the API — 409.
Past time: ← to yesterday — read-only; today past cells are grey.
Weekends: go to Saturday — a “Weekend” banner, creation disabled.
Load error: enable Offline in DevTools and change the date — “Retry” appears.
URL: switch to another day and reload — the day is kept.
Keys ← → T N, language and theme switches in the header; resize the window from phone to monitor.

sections.title: 11. Limitations and next steps
items: In-memory storage: resets on restart and is not shared between Vercel instances. Next step — Redis or a database.
No optimistic updates: a booking appears after the server responds (~0.4 s).
One room, no week view — the assignment asks for a day calendar.
CI (GitHub Actions with linters, unit and e2e) — next step.

sections.title: 12. Delivery (assignment)
items: Repository, README, deployed demo and AI chat — links below.
Time: about 4 hours of work with AI plus clarifications with the recruiter (within the 4–6 h timebox).
